questions.q: Why does the summary describe spending on employees as an investment?
a: Satisfied employees lead to satisfied customers and revenue
Higher pay always attracts the most talented applicants
Training costs are usually tax deductible for companies
Well-paid staff require less supervision from managers
questions.why: The overview says a healthy workplace makes employees productive and customers happy, which benefits the business.

questions.q: What is the first step in running an effective recruiting campaign?
a: Segment the audience and know who you are looking for
Offer the highest salary the budget can support
Post the vacancy on every available job board
Ask current employees to interview candidates
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to segment your audience first, considering the impact and scarcity of the skills you need.

questions.q: What is guerilla marketing in the context of hiring?
a: Using unconventional methods to grab people's attention
Buying expensive ads in national newspapers
Sending recruiters to competitors' offices
Holding interviews in public coffee shops
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines guerilla marketing as outside-the-box promotion that makes an audience more likely to engage.

questions.q: What does pipelining mean in the hiring process?
a: Filtering applicants by credentials to narrow the list
Training new hires before they start work
Promoting employees from within the company
Scheduling several rounds of group interviews
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes pipelining as using criteria such as credentials and experience to drop unsuitable candidates.

questions.q: What does the summary say about making a single good hire?
a: It cannot transform a company without consistent recruiting
It is enough to improve the whole organization's performance
It matters more than the company's financial resources
It should be avoided in favor of internal promotions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says one good hire will not make a company successful and that hiring must be consistent.
